text.p: Togo's parliament has approved a 1997 budget envisaging a deficit of 10.4 billion CFA francs, less than half the figure projected last year, to be financed from external sources.
The national assembly adopted the budget late on Monday by 44 votes to 32 with five abstentions.

The deficit is under half the 22 billion CFA forecast in the 1996 budget, but Prime Minister Kwassi Klutse said before Christmas that the outgoing year's final deficit would in fact be only 700 million CFA thanks to prudent management.
Revenue in the 1997 year beginning January 1 is forecast at 126.2 billion CFA and spending at 136.4 billion CFA.

Economy and Finance Minister Barry Moussa Barque said the difference would be covered by funding from a mix of external sources including the World Bank, the African Development Bank and the European Union.
The budget focuses on social spending, with increases for education and health. The government plans to scrap Value Added Tax for fertiliser, energy, medicines and water.
The main opposition Action Committee for Renewal (CAR) voted against the budget, saying it did nothing for unemployment.
Former prime minister Edem Kodjo and his supporters abstained, saying that there was lack of clarity over where certain revenue would come from.
